target.title: Fix failed automerge session reconciliation
target.body:
## Summary

- add `repair_failed` as an automerge terminal outcome when the linked repair workflow ends with `failure`, `timed_out`, or `action_required`
- reconcile PR merged/closed state first, then validate the linked run repository, URL, and `repair-cluster-worker.yml` identity before terminalizing an open PR session
- report failures best-effort from the repair workflow while keeping the seven-day scheduled reconcile as a fallback
- expose the new outcome in the dashboard and include it automatically in terminal success-rate calculations
- add single-session reconciliation, JSON output, help text, explicit exit codes, and conservative handling of invalid input or network failures

## Root cause

Terminal reconciliation only inspected the target PR's `merged_at` and `closed_at`. When the PR remained open but its linked repair workflow had already failed, the session stayed in `repairing` indefinitely and never entered the success-rate denominator.

## Safety and behavior

- merged and closed PR state takes precedence over repair-run conclusions
- cancelled, neutral, skipped, successful, and in-progress repair runs do not map to `repair_failed`
- successful requeue dispatches prevent the old session from being terminalized by the failed run
- direct reporting and scheduled reconciliation use the same outcome-specific idempotency event ID
- no KV migration or manual live data mutation is required

## Validation

- `pnpm run check`
- `/data/code/openclaw/openclaw/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output`
  - clean: no accepted/actionable findings

target.title: fix(apply): preserve runtime yields across coverage proof
target.body:
## Summary

- preserve `GitHubRuntimeBudgetError` through coverage-proof hydration and execution
- propagate runtime-budget exhaustion from the post-proof canonical PR safety recheck
- prevent a slow GitHub read from recording a business `kept_open`/retry result before the resumable runtime yield

## Root cause

The apply runtime reserves time to flush a resumable report. Coverage-proof catch blocks and the later canonical-PR recheck could treat that reserved-budget exception as an ordinary GitHub read/proof failure. Under coverage instrumentation, the slow path crossed the reserve boundary and emitted the wrong action before yielding.

## Validation

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false run check`
- target regression repeated 3x normally and 3x with `--experimental-test-coverage`
- commit-range gitleaks: no leaks
- autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings

This is an independent CI/runtime fix discovered while validating #670; it intentionally does not include the automerge E2E fixture changes.
